earlier_scan.source_named: Yang, Cathryn (2015). Lalo Dialects Across Time and Space: Subgrouping, Dialectometry, and Intelligibility. Asia-Pacific Linguistics 22, ANU — covers Lalo phonology (tonal); repository not fetchable here.

sources.citation: Lama, Ziwo Qiu-Fuyuan. 2012. Subgrouping of Nisoic (Yi) languages. PhD dissertation, University of Texas at Arlington. (Laluba/Weishan Wuyin Baiwudi profile, after TBL 1992: 685)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Weishan Laluba: 43 initials, 17 vowels, 3 tones (55, 33, 13/21); the word 'stress' does not occur in the dissertation.

sources.citation: Hu, Suhua & Andrew Simpson. 2024. Floating quantifiers, specificity and focus in Lalo Yi. Journal of East Asian Linguistics 33. doi:10.1007/s10831-023-09272-8 (open access)
sources.note: Syntax paper; only 'floating quantifiers are prosodically prominent (attract stress)'; no word-stress statement; variety not localised (Hu's Lalo is West Mountain per Yang's Table 1-2 'Hu and Duan 2000, Ma'anshan').

sources.citation: Yang, Cathryn. 2015. Lalo dialects across time and space: subgrouping, dialectometry, and intelligibility. Asia-Pacific Linguistics A-PL 22. Canberra: ANU. 260 pp. hdl:1885/95391
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 3.2.1 'Central East Mountain: Yong'an (CE-YA)' pp. 40-42 (the Dongshanba variety): segmental inventories and 5 tone categories (55, 24, 21, 33, harsh 21/33); no word-stress statement. Only incidental use of 'stressed' in the West Mountain CW-QY sketch p. 39: 'Following a stressed syllable, the syllabic nasal loses its syllabicity and merges with the previous syllable, as in yesterday /a2 n33/ > [ang33].' No placement rule anywhere (a full-text search for stress/accent full text: stress/accent/prominence).

sources.citation: Namkung, Ju (ed.). 1996. Phonological inventories of Tibeto-Burman languages. STEDT Monograph 3. Berkeley. LALO pp. 203-205 (after Chen 1986 and after Bjorverud 1994 'The phonology of Lalo', Longjie).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Syllable canon CV-T and N-T; tones high 55, mid 33, low 21, laryngealised 33/22; notes on syllabic nasal and morpheme fusion; nothing on stress.
